newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fyffes sells banana firm stake to Dole unit.
newsitem.headline: Fyffes sells banana firm stake to Dole unit.

text.p: Irish fruit wholesaler and distributor Fyffes Plc said on Thursday that it has sold its 50 percent shareholding in the Banana Trading Corporation for a total consideration of $26.3 million.

Fyffes said in a statement that it sold its stake to a wholly-owned subsidiary of Dole Food Company Inc and has entered into new long-term shipping agreements with Dole regarding the shipping of part of its banana requirements from Latin America.
Fyffes said the shipping agreements would be of benefit to Fyffes and Dole and would give both companies significant scale economies.
"We are pleased to have entered these new shipping agreements which we believe will be mutually beneficial," Fyffes deputy chairman Carl McCann said.

Fyffes said the $26.3 million consideration for its stake in the Banana Trading Corporation included the repayment of debt due to Fyffes. Of the total proceeds, $19.3 million will be received immediately with a further $7.0 million payable within four months.
The proceeds equate to the book value of the assets involved, Fyffes said.
Banana Trading Corporation owns a Guatemalan banana farming business along with other related assets including certain banana farming assets in Honduara.

"The assets sold have principally been employed in supplying the Fyffes' U.S. marketing operations which have been unprofitable and consequently the group has decided to dispose of them," McCann said.
He said the cash generated would be used to continue Fyffes' programme of European expansion and the group expected these transactions to be earnings enhancing in 1997.
